title: Listening as love
hook: listening may be love's most common form

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was small acts: drops that fill the pot over time. Your line was small things.

Halfway through a friend's story, a sentence starts forming. A better story. A piece of advice. The same thing happened to me. The friend is still talking, but the mind has already left the room to rehearse. It's a moment with two sides: the one waiting to speak, and the one who can tell they're not really being heard. Two old texts, from the letter of James and from the book of Job, point at another way to be in a conversation.
screen: `A SENTENCE STARTS FORMING.` → `THE MIND LEAVES THE ROOM.` → `ANOTHER WAY TO BE THERE.`

segments.voice: First, the order of things. The letter of James, in the King James Bible, puts it in a single line: "let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath." Swift to hear comes first. Not clever to answer. Not quick with advice. The ears come ahead of the mouth. Second, a picture of it done well. In the book of Job, everything has been taken from Job: his children, his health, his wealth. Three friends come to comfort him, and at first they do something remarkable. "So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great." They don't explain. They don't fix. They stay. Third, what happens next. Eventually the friends start talking, for chapters, explaining why this must have happened to him. Some readers notice that the friends were at their best in the silence, and went wrong when they started to speak. At the end of the book, the text says God is not pleased with what they said about him. Fourth, a word from Hebrew that holds all of this. A prayer said in Jewish worship, from the book of Deuteronomy, begins with Shema: hear, or listen. In that prayer, listening comes first. Listening isn't a pause before the real love begins. It can be the love. Full attention says, without a single word, you matter enough for me to stop.
screen: `SWIFT TO HEAR, SLOW TO SPEAK.` · `THEY SAT WITH HIM ON THE GROUND.` · `WRONG WHEN THEY STARTED TO SPEAK.` · `SHEMA: HEAR.` · then, large: `LISTENING AS LOVE.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes, or let them rest low, and just listen: first the farthest sound you can hear, then something closer in the room, then the closest of all, your own breath, letting each arrive and leave without naming or judging it. When your mind starts composing something to say, notice it and come back to listening, the same muscle a friend needs from you. If you pray, you can listen in your own tradition's way.
Shema. The opening word of a Jewish prayer that means hear, or listen, placing attention before any answer. Today's word.
Your line: just listen. Sometimes the kindest answer is your full attention. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jews say the Shema, which opens with the word hear, in daily prayer; in Jewish mourning, by custom, visitors to a house of mourning wait for the mourner to speak first, and people on many paths practice listening as a form of care in chaplaincy and friendship.

chat.says: My friend's going through something awful. What should I say to him?
options: Maybe very little at first. Job's friends did best sitting with him in silence.
Explain why it probably happened, so he can make sense of it right away.
Have a better story ready while he talks, so you can jump in quickly.
